messages.subject: equation for exact matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
   Can someone please provide me with the equation for
exact matching? For example suppose I have two treatment cases
and 4 control cases and there is one covariate (X), where X=0,1. Suppose
that the treatment and control cases match exactly on X=1, how does
exact matching match the cases?

My reasoning is that it will match treatment case 1 to the 4 control  
cases
and treatment case 2  also to the four control cases. Therefore you have
two subclasses with a total of 10 cases. Am I correct?

George

messages.subject: Re: equation for exact matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi George,
As is mostly explained on this website, http://gking.harvard.edu/matchit/docs/Exact_Matching.html, exact matching will form subclasses such that within each subclass all of the subjects have the same values on the covariates.

In your little example, if I read it correctly, if everyone has X=1 then there will be one subclass, and both treatment subjects and the 4 controls will all be in that subclass.  Otherwise if there is say 1 treated and 2 control with X=0 and 1 treated and 2 control with X=1 then it will form two subclasses, one for each of the two values of X.

Liz
